html:
A creole language that grew in Cape Verde in the 15th and 16th centuries, from Portuguese mixed with West African languages such as Wolof and Mandinka. It is among the oldest creoles still spoken.

It formed at Ribeira Grande, where Portuguese settlers and enslaved Africans from the Guinea coast lived together, and spread with traders to Guinea-Bissau, where a related creole is spoken. Portuguese stayed the language of school and state, but Kriolu is the language of home, of morna songs and of the large diaspora. Each island has its own variety. Writers have used it since the 19th century, and making it an official language is a long political debate.
